CONSULAAT-GENERAAL DER NEDERLANDEN
VOOR MIDDEN-CHINA.
TEL. AD. HOLLANDIA.

No.3751.                                        SHANGHAI,    7 November    1936 .
                                                **〔此处转录不清〕**

Sir,

    Further to my letter of September 20, 1936, No.3502 (your
reference 1.7045), I have the honour to inform you that according
to a report received from Hongkong Muliali alisa Mohamed Ali
alisa Sihombong Toeroenen has been repatriated to the Netherlands
Indies by the s.s. "Tjisalak", which left Hongkong on the third
of this month.

    There appeared to be no sufficient evidence against him to
warrant an order for his expulsion on account of communist in-
clinations, but since he had lost his position he was considered
an undesirable vagrant and after authority had been obtained from
the Netherlands Indian Government he was sent back for the said
Government's account.

    Measures were taken to prevent his landing at Muntok, the
only port of call between Hongkong and Batavia.

                                            I have the honour to be,
                                                    Sir,
                                            Your obedient servant,

                                            **〔签名〕**
                                            Chinese Secretary.


Major V.M.Bourne,
  Officer i/c Special Branch,
    Shanghai Municipal Police,
              SHANGHAI.

                                            P.P.
                                            Put up letter on
                                            acknowledgement.
                                            **〔印章：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / 10 NOV 1936〕**
                                            Done
                                            DBR.
                                            K/H

荷兰驻华中总领事馆
电话地址：HOLLANDIA。

第3751号。                                        上海，    1936年11月7日。
                                                **〔此处转录不清〕**

先生：

    继我1936年9月20日第3502号函（贵方参考号1.7045）之后，谨此通知您，根据从香港收到的报告，Muliali（又名Mohamed Ali，又名Sihombong Toeroenen）已由本月3日离开香港的“Tjisalak”号轮船遣返回荷属东印度。

    似乎没有足够的证据对他下达因共产主义倾向而驱逐的命令，但由于他已失业，被视为不受欢迎的流浪者，在获得荷属东印度政府授权后，由该政府出资将其遣返。

    已采取措施防止他在文岛（Muntok）登陆，这是香港与巴达维亚之间唯一的停靠港。

                                            谨此致意，
                                                    先生，
                                            您顺从的仆人，

                                            **〔签名〕**
                                            中文秘书。

V.M. Bourne少校，
  特别处主管，
    上海公共租界工部局警务处，
              上海。

                                            P.P.
                                            附上回执信函。
                                            **〔印章：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / 1936年11月10日〕**
                                            已办
                                            DBR.
                                            K/H

CONSULAAT-GENERAAL DER NEDERLANDEN
VOOR MIDDEN-CHINA.
TEL. AD. HOLLANDIA.

No. 3751.                                        SHANGHAI,    7 November    1936 .

Sir,

    Further to my letter of September 30, 1936, No. 3502 (your
reference I.7045), I have the honour to inform you that according
to a report received from Hongkong Mohamed Ali
alias Sihombing Toeroenan has been repatriated to the Netherlands
Indies by the s.s. "Tjibadak", which left Hongkong on the third
of this month.

    There appeared to be no sufficient evidence against him to
warrant an order for his expulsion on account of communist in-
clinations, but since he had lost his position he was considered
an undesirable vagrant and after authority had been obtained from
the Netherlands Indian Government he was sent back for the said
Government's account.

    Measures were taken to prevent his landing at Muntok, the
only port of call between Hongkong and Batavia.

                                            I have the honour to be,
                                                    Sir,
                                            Your obedient servant,

                                            Chinese Secretary.

Major V.M. Bourne,
    Officer i/c Special Branch,
        Shanghai Municipal Police,
                    SHANGHAI.

                                            P.P.
                                            Put up letter in
                                            acknowledgement.

                                            （印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE 10 NOV 1936）

                                            Done
                                            8/11.
                                            "J"

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Section 2, Special Branch
REPORT
File No. 7548
Date October 6, 36

Subject Letter from Netherlands Consulate-General re Netherlands suspects.

Made by D. S. Jones Forwarded by **〔此处转录不清〕**

In connection with attached communication No. 3392 dated
September 26, 1936 from the Netherlands Consulate General
I interviewed Mr. Van den Berg today and asked him if there
was anything the Special Branch could do with regard to check-
ing upon the activities of certain Netherlands subjects
mentioned in the letter. Mr. Van den Berg, who appreciated
the offer of assistance, stated that he did not wish the
Police to take any action in the matter, the object of the
letter being simply to keep this Branch informed of the
movements and possible subversive activities of various
Javanese suspects.

Mr. Van den Berg is in touch with Darwish, former
currycook of the Royal Hotel in Range Road. From him he
hopes to learn more about Hassan, the supposed master mind
of the group, referred to in the Netherlands Consulate letter.
Hassan is now in Tientsin. Although Darwish has denied all
connections with Hassan, there is definite proof that the
latter has been in correspondence with him over a considerable
period.

The addresses referred to as being contained "in the
writing book" are chiefly those of Javanese residing in the
Netherlands East Indies. The only Shanghai addresses are
those of tailors, three of which are established in Szechuen
Road, the remaining two in Bubbling Well Road and Carter Road.
No significance attaches to the finding of these Shanghai
addresses at the home of the Netherlands subject MALIAKI
alias Mohamed Ali alias Sihombong Toeroenan arrested in Hong-
kong on September 10, 1936. Maliaki was a tailor by trade
and came to Shanghai during June of 1935 in search of employment.

主题 关于荷兰嫌疑人的荷兰总领事馆来函。

制作人 D. S. Jones 转呈人 **〔此处转录不清〕**

就附上的1936年9月26日荷兰总领事馆第3392号公函而言，我今天会见了Van den Berg先生，询问特别处在核查信中提到的某些荷兰籍人员活动方面是否能有所作为。Van den Berg先生对提供的协助表示赞赏，但他表示不希望警方在此事上采取任何行动，该函的目的仅仅是让本处了解各种爪哇嫌疑人的动向和可能的颠覆活动。

Van den Berg先生与Darwish保持联系，后者曾是兰心路（Range Road）皇家酒店（Royal Hotel）的咖喱厨师。他希望通过Darwish了解更多关于Hassan的情况，据荷兰领事馆信函所述，Hassan是该团伙所谓的幕后主脑。Hassan目前在天津。尽管Darwish否认与Hassan有任何联系，但有确凿证据证明后者在相当长的一段时间内一直与他通信。

信中提及包含在“写字簿”中的地址主要是居住在荷属东印度的爪哇人的地址。唯一的上海地址是裁缝的地址，其中三家位于四川路，另外两家位于静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）和卡特路（Carter Road）。1936年9月10日在香港被捕的荷兰籍人员MALIAKI（又名Mohamed Ali，又名Sihombong Toeroenan）家中发现这些上海地址并无特殊意义。Maliaki职业为裁缝，于1935年6月来到上海寻找工作。

CONSULAAT-GENERAAL DER NEDERLANDEN
VOOR MIDDEN-CHINA.
TEL. AD. HOLLANDIA.

No. 3392.                                      SHANGHAI,
                                               26 September 1936.

Sir,
    I have the honour to inform you that I am in receipt of
a communication from Hongkong to the effect that the Colonial
Police arrested there on the 10th of this month the Nether-
lands subject MALIAKI alias MOHAMED ALI alias SIHOMBONG
TOEROENAN, holder of a Netherlands Indian passport No. 830-1934,
issued at Medan (Sumatra, N.I.) on August 1, 1934 for the
voyage to the Straits Settlements, the Federated Malay States
and back to the Netherlands Indies. This passport was extended
by this Consulate-General on November 2, 1935 and made valid then
until August 1, 1936. According to this passport the holder was
born at Litonguikoeta, Tapanoeli, Sumatra, 24 years of age,
domiciled at Medan and of the Protestant religion.
    According to the records of this Consulate-General Maliaki
(and not Maliali as reported) arrived in Shanghai in Juni 1935
and registered here on October 12, 1935, stating that he was
both a sailor and a tailor. His father's name was said to be
Conrad, that of his mother Artina, whereas he was supposed to
be a resident of Boeloedoeri, Onderafdeeling Sidikarang,
Darilanden, Tapanoeli.
    Whilst in Shanghai he seems to have been employed by
Ahmid Din Sons, 473 Bubbling Well Road and by Percy, 327
Szechuen Road.

                                               In

T. Robertson, Esquire,
    Deputy Commissioner (Special Branch),
        Shanghai Municipal Police,
            SHANGHAI.

先生，
    谨此通知您，我收到来自香港的公函，称殖民地警察于本月10日在那里逮捕了荷兰籍人员MALIAKI（又名MOHAMED ALI，又名SIHOMBONG TOEROENAN），其持有荷属东印度护照第830-1934号，该护照于1934年8月1日在棉兰（苏门答腊，荷属东印度）签发，用于前往海峡殖民地、马来联邦及返回荷属东印度的旅程。本总领事馆于1935年11月2日对该护照进行了延期，使其有效期延至1936年8月1日。根据该护照，持照人出生于苏门答腊塔帕努里（Tapanoeli）的Litonguikoeta，年龄24岁，寓所位于棉兰，信仰新教。
    根据本总领事馆的记录，Maliaki（而非报告中所述的Maliali）于1935年6月抵达上海，并于1935年10月12日在此注册，声称自己既是水手又是裁缝。据说其父名为Conrad，其母名为Artina，而他被认为是塔帕努里达里兰登（Darilanden）Sidikarang分区Boeloedoeri的居民。
    在上海期间，他似乎受雇于静安寺路473号的Ahmid Din Sons公司和四川路327号的Percy公司。

                                               In

T. Robertson先生，

pages.en:
- 2 -

In 1936 he was living at 521 Woosung Road, the same
address where Raden Mashoed, mentioned in my letter of
October 9th, 1935, No. 3337, and Item and Bong, two persons
who arrived here as stowaways from Sumatra in the beginning
of this year, have been living.

Mohamed Ali approached this Consulate-General a few
times for assistance in finding employment or for funds to
enable him to leave Shanghai.

As far as I can find out he left Shanghai on or about
the 17th of March of this year, when he called at my office
and produced a ticket on a steamer to Hongkong.

Mohamed Ali appears to have found employment in Hongkong
with a British Indian tailor at 24 Queen's Road, but was
arrested on account of his being in possession of a passport
which was not longer valid and of his failure to register
himself.

According to a report in the North China Morning Post
of September 14, 1936 Mohamed Ali was fined $ 10.-, in
default a week's hard labour, with an expulsion order to
follow.

On his house being searched a writing-book containing
addresses, two small note-books, a photo. album and a number
of letters and papers were seized. The letters showed that
he was in communication with P. Darwish, the former currycook
of the Royal Hotel, at present unemployed and with J. Hassan,
who is at present in Tientsin.

These letters are written in Malay. According to the
English translation thereof Darwish amongst other things
states "I must remain in Shanghai for one or two years until
some one from Indonesia with the same intentions as ours
arrives
pages.zh:
- 2 -

1936年，他居住在吴淞路521号，这也是我在1935年10月9日第3337号函中提到的Raden Mashoed，以及今年年初作为偷渡客从苏门答腊抵达此地的Item和Bong两人的居住地。

Mohamed Ali曾几次向本总领事馆求助，寻求就业帮助或资金以便离开上海。

据我所知，他于今年3月17日左右离开上海，当时他来到我的办公室，出示了一张前往香港的轮船船票。

Mohamed Ali似乎在香港皇后大道24号的一位英属印度裁缝处找到了工作，但因持有不再有效的护照且未进行登记而被捕。

根据1936年9月14日《华北明星报》（North China Morning Post）的报道，Mohamed Ali被罚款10元，若无力支付则服苦役一周，随后将执行驱逐令。

在搜查其住所时，查获了一本含有地址的写字簿、两本小笔记本、一本相册以及若干信件和文件。信件显示，他与目前失业的皇家酒店前咖喱厨师P. Darwish，以及目前在天津的J. Hassan有通信往来。

这些信件是用马来语写的。根据其英文译文，Darwish在其中 stating “我必须在上海停留一两年，直到某个与我们意图相同的印尼人到来

pages.en:
- 3 -

arrives to take my place", whereas Hassan in a letter to Mohamed
Ali dated May 29, 1936, writes "the result of my stay in Nanking
has not amounted too much, because I have'nt got the sympathy
of the Chinese leaders in awakening the Asian Unity".

Darwish mentions Hassan frequently in his letters although
he has always denied that he knew him or had any dealings with
him. The addresses contained in the writing-book make the
impression of having been copied from an existing list of addresses.
Copies of these addresses are now in my possession and available
for inspection.

There was also a picture found of Darwish (in scout's uni-
form), Raden Mashed and Mohamed Ali, on the reverse of which
was also written the address : 321 (521 ?) Woosung Road.

On March 15, 1936, Percy, of 327 Szechuen Road, appears to
have given Mohamed Ali a testimonial to the effect that he had
been working there for four months. His name is given therein
as Malaki Sikombing. The date of issue coincides with that of
his departure from Shanghai. Furthermore a postcard was found
on him, sent by B. Affendy, 200 B. Transfer Road, Penang, who
congratulates "Mohamed Ali" on his convertion to the Islam.

I am inclined to believe that the political activities of
this group are of a less dangerous nature than would appear
from their correspondence and that economic necessity has con-
tributed mainly to their associating together in China. It
would appear to me that in case they would have formed part of
a powerful organisation their financial position would not have
brought them into contact with the authorities. Even Hassan,
who is supposed to be the master mind of this group, seems to
have been in bad financial straits, and whatever revolutionary
ideas he may entertain, his contact with these persons has not
failed
pages.zh:
- 3 -

来取代我的位置”，而哈桑（Hassan）在1936年5月29日致穆罕默德·阿里（Mohamed Ali）的信中写道：“我在南京逗留的结果并无太大成效，因为我未能获得中国领导人在唤醒亚洲团结方面的同情。”

达尔维什（Darwish）在信中频繁提及哈桑，尽管他始终否认认识哈桑或与其有任何往来。记事本中所载的地址给人留下的印象是抄自一份现有的地址清单。这些地址的副本现由我持有，可供查阅。

此外还发现一张达尔维什（身着童子军制服）、拉登·马谢德（Raden Mashed）和穆罕默德·阿里的合影，照片背面亦写有地址：吴淞路321号（521号？）。

1936年3月15日，四川路327号的珀西（Percy）似乎向穆罕默德·阿里出具了一份证明，称其已在那里工作了四个月。证明中将其姓名列为马拉基·西孔宾（Malaki Sikombing）。签发日期与其离开上海的日期相符。此外，在他身上还发现一张明信片，系由槟城B. Transfer路200号的B. Affendy寄出，祝贺“穆罕默德·阿里”皈依伊斯兰教。

我倾向于认为，该团体的政治活动性质并不如其通信所显示的那般危险，经济需求主要是他们在中国聚集在一起的原因。在我看来，假如他们是某个强大组织的一部分，他们的财务状况就不会导致他们与当局发生接触。即便是被视为该团体智囊的哈桑，似乎也陷入严重的财务困境，而且无论他怀有何种革命思想，他与这些人的接触都未能

pages.en:
- 4 -

failed to expose him.
    I will try to get into touch with Darwish again and see
whether in the face of the evidence, now available against
him, he will still deny all connections with Hassan.
                        I have the honour to be,
                                Sir,
                        Your obedient servant,
                        〔此处转录不清〕
                        Chinese Secretary.
pages.zh:
- 4 -

使他免于暴露。
    我将尝试再次与达尔维什取得联系，看看在面对目前掌握的对他的证据时，他是否仍会否认与哈桑的所有联系。
                        谨此致意，
                                先生，
                        您顺从的仆人，

                        华务秘书。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. 7545
Section 2, Special Branch 8/10/36 C L
REPORT
Date September 30, 36

Subject Communication dated September 18, 1936 from H.B.M. Consulate-
General regarding once Percy C. Ho.
Made by D. S. Pitts Forwarded by J. Logan D.S.I.

Percy C. Ho's correct name is Ho Pah Chi(賀伯琪); a
native of Szechuen, he is about 33 years of age and is at
present residing at Passage 190, House No. 18 Route Picard
Destelan (Telephone No. 70678).

Educated and brought up by missionaries, Ho arrived in
Shanghai from Szechuen in 1925 and during the same year obtain-
ed a position as a clerk with Messrs. C.N. Gray & Co., 181
Nanking Road. Later he was appointed accountant in the
same concern, remaining there until 1930 when he resigned.
During his period of employment with Messrs. C. N. Gray & Co.
Ho naturally acquired a great deal of knowledge about the
tailoring trade, and in 1930 established his own tailoring
and outfitting shop at 88 Kiangse Road, under the name of
PERCY THE TAILOR, financial support being supplied by a French-
man connected with Messrs. Olivier-Chine (S.A.), 95 Museum Road.
Ho later removed his establishment to 81 Szechuen Road, and is
now located at 15 Ezra Road. He caters mostly for foreigners
of the Latin type, and a number of Hai Alai players and French-
men are regular customers. The greater part of his materials
are imported from France, probably due to the influence of his
sleeping French partner.

Ho appears to be quite well off financially, as he owns
a car and lives in a manner that indicates that he is free from
any money worries.

Ho has been charged, found guilty and fined on four
different occasions before the First Shanghai Special District
Court in respect of motoring offences.

He is on very friendly terms with one J. D. Zee, a
partner of the Mercantile Service Bureau, 330 Szechuen Road,

特科第二股 1936年10月8日 C L
报告
日期 1936年9月30日

事由 英国驻上海总领事馆1936年9月18日关于珀西·C·何先生的来函。
由 D. S. Pitts 撰写，由副督察 J. Logan 转呈。

珀西·C·何的真名为贺伯琪（Ho Pah Chi）；四川人，现年约33岁，目前居住于毕卡第公寓（Route Picard Destelan）18号190弄（电话70678）。

何氏由传教士抚养教育，1925年从四川来到上海，并于同年在南京路181号的C.N. Gray & Co.公司获得职员职位。后来他被任命为该公司的会计，一直任职至1930年辞职。在C. N. Gray & Co.公司任职期间，何氏自然积累了大量关于裁缝行业的知识，并于1930年在江西路88号开设了自己的裁缝及服饰店，店名为“PERCY THE TAILOR”（珀西裁缝店），资金由一位与奥利弗-中国公司（Olivier-Chine (S.A.)，博物馆路95号）有关的法国人提供。何氏后来将店铺迁至四川路81号，现位于爱兹拉路15号。他的顾客多为拉丁裔外国人，许多海莱（Hai Alai）球员和法国人是其常客。他的大部分面料从法国进口，这可能受到其隐名法国合伙人的影响。

何氏的经济状况似乎相当宽裕，因为他拥有一辆汽车，且生活方式表明他没有任何金钱烦恼。

何氏曾在第一上海特区地方法院因交通违章被起诉、定罪并罚款四次。

他与J. D. Zee关系非常友好，后者是四川路330号商业服务局（Mercantile Service Bureau）的合伙人，
